evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check only requires nonzero, different manager PIDs and invocation IDs. It never verifies that the before/after manager snapshots come from the same boot, even though the snapshot data already carries `boot_id` (as used by `boot_id_changed`). A guest reboot between the two manager snapshots can change both PID and invocation ID, making `manager_restarted` pass across a reboot; the later planned reboot still satisfies `boot_id_changed`, so nothing rejects the confounded manager-restart evidence. Adding a nonempty/equal boot-ID condition for the manager snapshot pair is a routine correctness repair, not a new requirement.
